## What’s All This Hype With AI?
The hype about artificial intelligence (AI) has reached new heights, with excitement around what organizations can achieve with [generative AI](https://www.blueprism.com/guides/ai/generative-ai/), predictive AI and whatever comes next. Everyone in Silicon Valley and beyond is grabbing a piece of the AI pie. But does AI really live up to the hype, or is reality a little more complicated?

We’ll look at:

- What a technology hype cycle is.
- How generative AI and predictive AI can work together.
- How AI is evolving across the business sphere.
- Where we can expect [businesses to gain the most from AI](https://www.blueprism.com/guides/ai/business-ai/).

## Why Is There So Much AI Hype?
Anyone who has had an eye on tech trends over the years knows the familiar cycle, illustrated in [Gartner’s Hype Cycle](https://www.gartner.com/en/articles/what-s-new-in-artificial-intelligence-from-the-2023-gartner-hype-cycle):

1. **Innovation trigger:** A new technology emerges.
2. **Peak of inflated expectations** **:** Companies heavily promote the new tech, overexposing it in the market.
3. **Trough of disillusionment** **:** Users get fatigued from seeing the tech and it eventually reaches unmet expectations and falls out of the spotlight.
4. **Plateau of productivity:** The tech reaches some mainstream real-world use cases.

In the latest gen AI hype cycle, we entered the trough of disillusionment, in part due to gen AI projects failing to deliver value because of a solution looking for a problem, poor data quality, inadequate risk controls, escalating costs and failing to define the business return on investment (ROI) linkage.

## AI hype
Let’s start with the big question: What’s the big deal with AI? We’re seeing it filter into everyday life, from the advertisements we see on the mega screens to the tiny computers living inside our smart watches.

More and more companies want to sell AI to us in some shape or form. While part of this sudden promotion has to do with using trendy keywords to garner the attention of the masses, AI has its place and _can_ be useful in a business setting.
